items.reason: Lift flows from the preset through build options to row ordering and marking.
Only the shipped active preset enables Lift.
The pin alias sets the same field without emitting findings or notices.
Decoding lift after pin gives lift precedence.
An undeclared grant defaults to false.
Invalid values for either spelling produce findings without failing loading.
Derived-ordering identifiers, comments, and test filenames consistently use lift.
Manual and unrelated pin terminology and behavior remain unchanged.
The field tag, description, and shipped presets use lift; pin is decode-only.
Repository attribution reaches bound sets from sibling worktrees.
Checkout attribution retains its existing ranking and returns before repository attribution.
Task-set tags retain precedence over repository answers.
The repository index includes both bound and unbound Task sets.
Repository attribution indexes and matches canonical git common directories.
Task-set and Map cursor keys still use project name and identifier; collisions make lifting select another repository’s row.
Missing or unknown repository identities yield no attribution or message.
Repository answers concatenate in kind precedence order, with a two-kind assertion.
Launch resolves repository identity once; a counting git test covers five rebuilds.
Status builds with empty pane facts and performs no attribution git lookup.
Lifting operates only on admitted rows, preserving preset narrowing.
Repository attribution includes live Maps and excludes abandoned or broken Maps.
Combined attribution lifts Task sets before Maps, covered by a shared-repository test.
Map session stamps return before the weaker repository pass.
Routines implement neither locality seam, with an explicit explanation of the asymmetry.

scores.rationale: Clear implementation and broad behavioral tests, but repository isolation fails for duplicate identities and lacks the required collision coverage.
